samples.identification: Synthetic NanoCoreUltimate .NET stealer with lockout, propagation and extortion routines
evidence: CLR entry token 0x0600001d / Program.Main RVA 0x2188 directly starts persistence, keyboard capture and worker tasks; no string obfuscation is needed to recover the IL.

StartKeylogger RVA 0x35e8 installs hook type 13 and also starts a GetAsyncKeyState polling loop. HookCallback RVA 0x3720 records timestamp, active-window title and virtual key in a StringBuilder. FlushKeylog RVA 0x37f0 sends a KEYLOG record via SendToC2.

SendToC2 RVA 0x5ff8 appends records locally, then passes its argument to WebClient.UploadString at http://xoilaclzxe.com. IsPlaceholder always returns true and disables some URL-building/beacon helpers, but does not gate this direct upload.
ContinuousScreenshot RVA 0x3a90 captures the primary display, saves JPEG, reads bytes, Base64-encodes and passes a SCREEN record to SendToC2; loop waits 30000 ms.
HighLevelFileStealer MoveNext RVA 0x3bac enumerates selected extensions in user folders, reads files, stages up to 1024 bytes under a .stolen name and sends FILE records. It repeats after 300000 ms.

SelfReplicate RVA 0x42f8 copies Application.ExecutablePath under system-like names, then to removable drives and writes executable AutoRun configurations. InstallPersistence RVA 0x3450 registers the current image in HKCU/HKLM Run and creates logon/repeating scheduled tasks.
BypassUAC RVA 0x5624 writes the executable to HKCU Software\Classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command, creates an empty DelegateExecute value, launches fodhelper.exe and schedules registry cleanup.

RealEncryption MoveNext RVA 0x4458 targets Desktop/TestFolder and attempts EncryptAES -> .encrypted write -> original deletion. The UTF-8 static key HiddenTearsKey123 is 17 bytes and IV H1ddenT3ars1v!! is 15 bytes, invalid for AES; set_Key throws before encryption. Ransom-note text does not establish successful encryption.

ProcessInjection MoveNext RVA 0x49a0 allocates/writes a one-byte RET (0xc3) in notepad and creates a remote thread. This demonstrates injection mechanics, without a concealment or hostile payload result. Existing neutral API-reference traits cover it.
Unrelated malware names and mutexes are planted. Self-ascribed NanoCore, HiddenTears, WannaCry and Remcos strings do not establish family lineage.

samples.identification: Floxif-infected Tonec Internet Download Manager IEMonitor 6.37.8.1
evidence: PE version resources describe Internet Download Manager agent for click monitoring in IE-based browsers. Tonec PKCS#7 signer cryptography verifies, but the image digest mismatches; this does not establish trusted executable bytes.

Entry VA 0x424007 is patched with a jump to 0x434cb1. Injected loader code walks the PEB and kernel export table to recover GetProcAddress. Helpers at 0x432af7 and 0x432b19 alter return addresses to jump over junk bytes.
The decryptor at VA 0x432b29 applies XOR plus bitwise complement, with a decoded flag. Stack-constructed API names are resolved dynamically.

Isolated Unicorn emulation with all external API calls stubbed traced loader VA 0x433319: read own file, decode appended payload, restore five original bytes under VirtualProtect, then try DLL paths including Common Files/System/symsrv.dll, System32/dlcoer.dll and Temp/conres.dll.

The loader WriteFile call at 0x434b4f (return 0x434b55) receives 69337 bytes beginning with MZ. Loader code subsequently resolves FloodFix2. Recovered DLL UPX-unpacks to 160473 bytes and exports FloodFix/FloodFix2.

Unpacked FloodFix2 VA 0x1000d728 changes PE-header protection, restores saved security-directory fields, writes saved code through the VirtualProtect/WriteProcessMemory helper at 0x10001ce4 and processes image relocation data. File-modification routines append multiple payload/length fields with WriteFile at 0x100058da..0x10005a6a and restore timestamps at 0x10005a86.

Host SetWindowsHookExA sites VA 0x40741e and 0x40ef7a pass hook types -1 (WH_MSGFILTER) and 5 (WH_CBT). These legitimate GUI hooks are not keyboard logging; registry/title APIs do not change that conclusion.

samples.identification: Native Protected Storage credential stealer and removable-drive AutoRun worm, recovered PE image
evidence: PE retains UPX0/UPX1/UPX2 labels and an old UPX entry stub, but UPX0 is populated with recovered code and runtime paths; some import/global-pointer areas retain resolved/obfuscated values. Treat as a recovered image, not proof of a successfully runnable fresh UPX archive.

Decoder VA 0x428653 XORs a NUL-terminated string in place; VA 0x428695 applies XOR over an explicit length. Call sites pass keys such as 2 and 5. For example the encoded Content-Type string decodes with XOR 2.

Drive replication thread VA 0x42a20c builds drive letters C..X, requires GetDriveType == 2, copies the current image to a drive-root executable, sets hidden/system attributes and writes autorun.inf line-by-line with an executable ShellExecute directive. The thread address is handed off at 0x42b32f.

Credential routine VA 0x42a4d4 loads pstorec.dll, resolves and calls PStoreCreateInstance, enumerates COM storage types/subtypes/items and formats password reports. pass_sites and auto_complete_pass paths call report formatting VA 0x42a48e, appending username/password records to global buffer 0x401000.
Wrapper VA 0x42acc8 returns that credential buffer. The worker calls it at 0x42b07b, encodes/appends changed report content, and calls HTTP sender VA 0x42964e at 0x42b13a.

HTTP sender constructs a form-urlencoded POST with the supplied body, connects a Winsock socket to port 80, then passes the built buffer to send at VA 0x4297ba. Embedded endpoints include bublikiadministrator.com and bublikimanager.com.

System-process image names are reference strings, not standalone masquerade evidence. There is no recovered WannaCry encryption behavior or basis to equate collector filename labels with family identity.
samples.marker: PStore AutoRun worm: relocate process-name references

scope: No fetched dependencies are involved. Original samples were never executed; native emulator external calls were intercepted with local stubs.
external_reports: Supplied tria.ge URLs were inaccessible. Decisions use local code, decoded payloads and data flow, not model scores or external family labels.

changes.false_positives: Require keyboard-specific hook and recording evidence; remove remote-API co-occurrence masquerading as hostile concealment. File-crypto/ransom-demand co-occurrence is suspicious extortion context, not successful encryption.
changes.missing_behaviors: Add managed file-data and screen-data upload profiles with independent keylog-theft admission, plus managed drive/AutoRun propagation context.
changes.taxonomy: Relocate system process name references, generic get_Headers token, policy paths/value names and analysis-tool references. Update exact consumers. Tool moves repair placement in the full process-name leaf before moving system names in; no directory budget was raised.
changes.severity: Raise complete Kill method-name and signer-verification observations to notable. The signed opaque-overlay/encoded-memory-API observation is suspicious anti-static context, not hostile signing-trust abuse.
changes.reference_audit: Audited exact and ancestor selectors. No behavioral ancestor consumer needed widening: moved recording stays within collection, removed encryption co-occurrence is replaced in impact, and generic names remain neutral. The metadata/file/policy/identity directory exclusion in the JavaScript scanner-blind rule uses unrelated metadata types; moved PE-only policy strings were ineligible there. Existing registry and anti-static ancestors already reference the same subjects.

validation.regression: 9 cases, 59 trait assertions passed. Two synthetic neutral/near-miss PE controls; three originals; four same-size record/directive mutations. check.py regenerates controls without saving malware in the repository.
